Ruling: model error; the reply counts the business cost of 2025 property used 50% or less in the business as section 179 property cost. i4562 p. 3, Part I: section 179 property must be "used predominantly (more than 50%) in your trade or business"; p. 4, Line 2, "Enter the total cost of all section 179 property you placed in service during the tax year". The reply's note shows it read the more-than-50% test as a condition of the election only. Ruling: scope; i4562 p. 7, Election out: "You can elect, for any class of property, to not deduct any special depreciation allowance for all such property in such class placed in service during the tax year." The candidate's screen adds a refusal for property placed in service in 2025 whose class has no uniform special-allowance choice (h_this_year and bonus_same false) and narrows acquired_before_bonus_date to property placed in service in 2025. The project computes the allowance on asset.bonus and asset.bonus_same and keeps the other property of the class on its 100%/40% path, so no computed amount differs; the same screen disagreement was ruled scope on 2026-11-16 (reviews/2025/transcription/adjudication/asset.md), and this reply reaches it from the same triage witnesses. Triage executable-triage-v2 (triage/asset.json): 1,157 of 2,715 comparisons agree; the 6 completed-return witnesses are single properties with bonus_choice none and the fixture default bonus_same false, project false / candidate true. Project stands.

Ruling: representation; the reply's (c) is i4562's column (c) after the reductions (p. 11, Column (c), "multiply the cost or other basis of the property by the percentage of business/investment use. From that result, subtract any credits and deductions allocable to the property", the section 179 deduction among them, and the special allowance), which the project carries as 19(c); the project's (c) is the business-use cost before them, as its label says.
